newsitem.title: USA: NHL ICE HOCKEY-FLYERS CENTER PROSPAL OUT FOR PLAYOFFS WITH BROKEN WRIST.
newsitem.headline: NHL ICE HOCKEY-FLYERS CENTER PROSPAL OUT FOR PLAYOFFS WITH BROKEN WRIST.

text.p: The Philadelphia Flyers, who take on the Buffalo Sabres in an NHL Eastern Conference semifinal series starting Saturday, learned on Wednesday they will be without potent rookie Vaclav Prospal.
Prospal, nicknamed "Vinny," sustained a broken left wrist at Wednesday's practice and the team said he will not return this season.

The 6-2 (1.88 m), 190-pounder (86 kg) centre played 18 games for the Flyers and had five goals and 10 assists, anchoring the second line and taking pressure off the "Legion of Doom" line of Eric Lindros, John LeClair and Mikael Renberg.

The Flyers went only 8-7-3 with him in the lineup down the stretch but Lindros missed a number of those games. Prospal had a goal and three assists for the Flyers in their five-game series win over the Pittsburgh Penguins in the first round of playoffs, registering 10 shots on goal.
The 22-year-old Prospal was leading the American Hockey League in scoring with 95 points on 32 goals and 63 assists in 63 games when he was recalled from the Philadelphia Phantoms.
